content: Hi everyone, as more people join the porting effort, I suggest we adopt a more open and organised approach to coordinating and tracking progress beyond PORTING.md. A simple and obvious option is to use the GitHub issue tracker. We can start by creating a ticket for each unfinished item in PORTING.md and marking it as assigned when someone takes on the task. In the future, we could also label the issues to categorise them and set up dependencies. If this sounds reasonable, I’ll look into it.
You can copy the approach Pietro and I used for the equational theories project. Glad to set it up if there is enough interest.
The implementation consists of a GitHub project, some basic task setup and CI automation for the rest

I agree that it would be great to have a more organized approach for tracking the porting. I think simply using issues is might be enough for the moment, but if there is a nicer approach that is not too tricky to setup, that also sounds good. I guess this is how the porting dashboard would look like? https://github.com/users/teorth/projects/1
@Shreyas Srinivas Can you describe a bit more what the features of this dashboard are?
It's basically an automated kanban board

You put up tasks there as project maintainers. People can claim tasks in the first column with a comment "claim". If there's no one else with a standing claim to the task, the issue is assigned to the claiming user. They can also "disclaim" the task. Once someone is a assigned an issue, they can open a PR associated with the task.
If their PR passes CI and they have marked it for review, the task moves the to next column. I initially created a PR review column that we did not end up using in the ETP
But I think it will be a bit more handy in iris
The review passed queue is essentially identical to what github calls merge queue these days.
and once a PR is merged the task is considered complete which puts it in the final column

The way I recall setting it up, only issues posted by admins to the outstanding task column or marked project-task enter the project dashboard. So you have control over what tasks are relevant to the port
We did not use roadmaps, but you can also explicitly set target deadlines for large tasks you want to achieve: https://github.com/users/teorth/projects/1/views/4
Fwiw, setting this up is much simpler now than it was in the ETP. We already know what to do and I have gotten better at CI scripting.

You can also control spamming and ensure that someone who claims a task gets to work on it in peace since they have a claim to it. The assumption here is that as maintainers you commit to merging PRs from this project board. So there’s no worry about someone scooping another person’s work and wasting their effort.

It usually requires little to no maintenance
Not more than CI usually does in general

Not more than CI usually does in general

I had a glance at the CI. It's a bit overwhelming to me... I think a cut-down version of it, with a simple dashboard and basic automation, should be good. But it seems like GitHub project is not available for iris-lean.

@Mario Carneiro, what do you think of this idea, and can you enable it?
Seems like a solution looking for a problem to be honest...
The ETP CI is large for different reasons

Many of the CI scripts that are included in the lean-action repository were not standard back then. The ETP CI also runs the blueprint, external checker(s), a bunch of tools to produce visualisations and equations search. You only need a small subset of it.

As the first step, I’ve created issues for all unchecked items (except for those in the Examples section) in PORTING.md with a script. I apologise for the spam to those subscribed to the repo activities.

Great :+1: I will see if I can later make a pass over the issues to group them more coherently than purely at the file level, at least for the places I know. (Not all features are perfectly scoped to a single file, so I think it makes sense to combine / split some issues to represent more high-level features than porting single files.)
Yep, good idea, especially for the proof mode ones.
Thanks for doing this!

I looked into the issues and slightly tweaked some. After thinking about this, I am not fully sure how to best proceed with the issues. Overall, I like that there is one issue per (Rocq) file since it makes it quite easy to find the issue for a feature (i.e., one can look at where the feature is implemented in Rocq and then look at the issue for the corresponding file) and for some things, this is very clear. However, there are issues like https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/issues/239 or https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/issues/213 which contain multiple features that will be ported independently. I was thinking about creating separate issues for such features (e.g. implementing the iframe tactic or some intropattern). I think this would be nice, but would blow up the number of issues and would require quite a bit of work to make sure all issues are linked correctly to each other. I am not sure if I have the time to do this with the necessary amount of care at this point. Maybe one can do this lazily? (E.g. when one starts to implement a tactic like iframe one can create an issue for it and link it from https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/issues/239 and other relevant issues)

Also with the issues we need to make sure to keep them up to date. I guess at the moment, we should keep both PORTING.md and the issues up to date and in sync, but if we stick with the issues, we might want to get rid of PORTING.md.

I hope it is not too much extra work. I'm not sure about removing PORTING.md though, unless we have a better alternative, e.g. a GitHub project, that can provide a good overview.
